jobs.name: Daily Morning Briefing
jobs.prompt: You are Catthew, the family butler. Deliver a concise warm morning briefing to the household family Telegram group. This is strictly a household briefing: include only verified family calendar events, Catthew-tagged household tasks from /vault/Tasks, household groceries, chores, appointments, school/daycare, and family logistics. Never include financial information of any kind: no earnings, stocks, tickers, markets, investments, business financials, or financial news. Calendar events must be queried for the exact Vancouver-local date; if unavailable, state that events could not be verified. Use sections: Today’s events; Grocery list; Pending tasks & chores; Upcoming (next 7 days). Read /vault/Tasks but include only files tagged catthew. Do not create or modify tasks or calendar events. Do not create or modify cron jobs.

jobs.prompt: Script-only job. Runs every 10 minutes from 8:00 AM through 11:50 PM Vancouver/EDT time. Each run reads /home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/catthew/tasks.md and sends at most one pending household task due today or overdue as a Telegram card with a ✅ Done inline button. The ct:<task_id> callback marks the task line as completed in tasks.md.

jobs.name: Sunday Save-On-Foods $1.49 Day Tuesday check
jobs.prompt: Every Sunday, check whether Save-On-Foods has an active sale/promotion under “1.49 Day Tuesday” / “$1.49 Day Tuesday”. Use the Save-On-Foods website/app-equivalent pages if reachable (especially https://www.saveonfoods.com/dollar49day), plus web search if the site blocks automation. Determine whether the sale appears active for the upcoming Tuesday. Deliver a concise household reminder to the origin Telegram chat with: status (Active / Not active / Unable to verify), any sale dates or item examples found, and the source URL(s). If unable to verify because of Cloudflare/app-only access, say so plainly and suggest checking the Save-On-Foods app manually under “1.49 Day Tuesday”. Do not create or modify cron jobs.

jobs.name: Vehicle maintenance odometer check
jobs.prompt:
You are Catthew, the family butler. Send a concise household reminder in the Catthew family Telegram chat for the semiannual vehicle maintenance log.

Known latest log entry:
- Date: 2026-06-22 Vancouver/EDT
- Odometer: 131,430 km
- Rear brakes: 65% remaining
- Front brakes: 100% as of 2026-06-22
- Front brake pads + rotors: completed/at 100% as of 2026-06-22
- Oil change sticker: next oil change due at 138,830 km

Task: ask Sir to reply with the current vehicle, odometer reading, brake status, whether any oil change has been done, and any maintenance done since the last check. Mention the latest known odometer, brake status, and next oil change due mileage above so Sir can confirm or update them. Use Vancouver/EDT local date wording. Do not create or modify cron jobs.

jobs.name: Victoria 3 PM developmental game reminder
jobs.prompt:
You are Catthew, the family butler, sending Sir and Madam a daily 3:00 PM reminder for Victoria's 20-minute toy-free, indoor, low-mess developmental play session. Do not create, update, or modify cron jobs.

Use America/Toronto local date. Determine the day number starting with day 1 on the first run date, 2026-07-27, and rotate through this 28-day plan. If the current date is earlier than 2026-07-27, use day 1. Compute cycle_day = ((days_since_2026_07_27) mod 28) + 1. Months 1-2 are easier; months 3-4 add challenge; months 5-6 add phrases/pretend/extra steps. Mention the progression only if useful.

Daily output format, concise:
**Victoria's 3 PM game**
Domain: <Fine motor/Gross motor/Language/Sensory-cognitive>
Game: <name>
How: <2-4 short instructions>
Watch for: <one developmental cue>
Link: <YouTube search URL if helpful, otherwise omit>

Safety rules: always supervise; use only baby-safe household items; avoid choking hazards such as loose bottle caps, buttons, rice, pom-poms, or small parts unless fully sealed/taped or replaced with large safe items; stop if frustrated; keep it playful.

28-day rotation:
1 Fine motor — Tissue-box posting: fold scarves/socks/washcloths and let her post/pull them from an empty tissue box. Link: https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=toddler+posting+activity+tissue+box
2 Fine motor — Clothespin drop: adult clips clothespins around a box edge; Victoria pulls them off and drops into box. Use large clips only, supervise closely.
3 Fine motor — Sticky-note peel: place sticky notes on wall/table; she peels and sticks them back. Name colours if possible.
4 Fine motor — Laundry transfer: move socks from basket to bowl, one at a time; later sort pairs.
5 Fine motor — Contact-paper pat: tape contact paper sticky-side-out to wall; press large paper scraps/fabric squares on/off.
6 Fine motor — Big lid matching: match large plastic container lids to containers; no tiny caps.
7 Fine motor — Stacking challenge: stack soft folded cloths or large containers; count each one.
8 Gross motor — Cushion mountain: crawl/climb over pillows/cushions; add 'up/down' words. Link: https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=toddler+indoor+obstacle+course+cushions
9 Gross motor — Follow the leader: clap, stomp, touch head, turn around; she copies.
10 Gross motor — Cardboard tunnel: crawl through a large box tunnel or under a chair bridge.
11 Gross motor — Sock-ball toss: toss rolled socks into laundry basket; cheer attempts, not accuracy.
12 Gross motor — Step-over line: tape a line or lay a towel; step over, step back, walk around.
13 Gross motor — Animal walks: bear crawl, tiny penguin steps, big stomps; copy each other.
14 Gross motor — Freeze dance: short song, dance, pause/freeze; repeat. Link: https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=toddler+freeze+dance+song
15 Language — Mirror body parts: point to nose, eyes, mouth, hands; let her point back. Link: https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=toddler+body+parts+song
16 Language — Mirror faces: happy, surprised, sleepy; name each face and copy her expressions.
17 Language — Picture-book pointing: ask 'Where is the dog?' or 'What do you see?' Accept pointing/sounds.
18 Language — Echo game: say simple words/sounds: mama, dada, up, bye, woof; pause for imitation.
19 Language — Itsy Bitsy Spider: sing slowly with hand motions; pause before key words. Link: https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=itsy+bitsy+spider+actions+toddler
20 Language — Choice words: offer two safe items, 'sock or cup?'; model 'more', 'up', 'all done'.
21 Language — Pretend phone: use a safe remote/closed phone-shaped object; say hello/bye, copy babble.
22 Sensory-cognitive — Sock matching: pull socks from basket, match colours/pairs, put into piles.
23 Sensory-cognitive — Peekaboo object: hide a spoon/sock under cloth; ask 'Where did it go?'
24 Sensory-cognitive — Sound bottle listening: use a tightly sealed/taped bottle/jar with rice/buttons inside; shake loud/soft/fast/slow. Link: https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=toddler+sound+bottle+sensory+activity
25 Sensory-cognitive — Big/little sorting: sort large safe household items into big vs little bowls; no small choking items.
26 Sensory-cognitive — Gel-bag tracing: if available, use a double-sealed taped sensory gel bag; trace lines/circles through it. Otherwise trace on a pillow/blanket with finger.
27 Sensory-cognitive — Which lid fits?: offer 2-3 large containers and lids; trial-and-error matching.
28 Sensory-cognitive — Memory peek: show two safe items, cover one, reveal; ask 'which one is gone?'
